Extract a task and archive its source reference in one atomic operation.

This tool does three things:
1. Adds the task to the shared extracted_tasks memory block (concurrent-safe).
2. Inserts a structured source reference passage into the shared
   extracted_tasks_archive (visible to all agents with the archive attached).
3. Optionally removes the source queue entry from a block (atomic cleanup).

The ref_id (8-char hex) links the two together.

Only capture metadata that is explicitly stated or clearly evident in the
source material. Do NOT infer or fabricate dates, priorities, or project
associations that are not present in the source.
tools.name: add_extracted_tasks
tools.source_code:
def add_extracted_tasks(
    task_description: str,
    source_type: str,
    source_context: str,
    reference_id: str,
    source_text: str,
    from_person: str,
    location: str,
    location_id: str,
    source_timestamp: str,
    project: Optional[str] = None,
    due_date: Optional[str] = None,
    defer_date: Optional[str] = None,
    priority: Optional[str] = None,
    related_urls: Optional[str] = None,
    origin: Optional[str] = None,
    estimate_minutes: Optional[int] = None,
    cleanup_block_id: Optional[str] = None,
    cleanup_entry_identifier: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Extract a task and archive its source reference in one atomic operation.

    This tool does three things:
    1. Adds the task to the shared extracted_tasks memory block (concurrent-safe).
    2. Inserts a structured source reference passage into the shared
       extracted_tasks_archive (visible to all agents with the archive attached).
    3. Optionally removes the source queue entry from a block (atomic cleanup).

    The ref_id (8-char hex) links the two together.

    Only capture metadata that is explicitly stated or clearly evident in the
    source material. Do NOT infer or fabricate dates, priorities, or project
    associations that are not present in the source.

    Args:
        task_description: Concise verb-led task title
            (e.g., "Review agenda items highlighted in yellow on worksheet").
        source_type: Source type shorthand. One of: "slack", "google-docs",
            "meeting", "email", "google-docs-comment".
        source_context: Human-readable origin description
            (e.g., "Direct message from Danielle Kehoe").
        reference_id: Deterministic canonical unique identifier for the source.
            Format depends on source_type:
            slack = "slack-{channel_id}-{ts}" or "slack-{channel_id}-{ts}-t{thread_ts}" if message was in a thread,
            google-docs = "gdocs-{document_id}",
            meeting = "meeting-{meeting_id}",
            email = "email-{message_id}",
            google-docs-comment = "gdocs-comment-{document_id}-{comment_id}".
        source_text: Verbatim relevant text from the source. Do NOT summarize.
        from_person: Person name or ID who originated the task
            (e.g., "Danielle Kehoe (U09B5JUK2TY)").
        location: Human-readable location: channel name, document URL,
            meeting title, or email subject line.
        location_id: Machine-readable location identifier: channel ID,
            document ID, meeting ID, or message ID.
        source_timestamp: When the source message or document was created,
            in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-02-11T06:37:00Z").
        project: Optional project name for tagging. Only provide if clearly
            relevant (e.g., "grants", "codap"). Adds a 4th tag.
        due_date: Optional due date in ISO 8601 format. Only provide when
            explicitly stated in source (e.g., "by Friday", "due March 1").
            Do NOT infer deadlines that are not clearly indicated.
        defer_date: Optional defer/start date in ISO 8601 format. Only provide
            when explicitly stated (e.g., "start Monday", "after the meeting").
        priority: Optional priority level. One of: "high", "normal", "low".
            Only provide when urgency is clearly indicated in the source
            (e.g., "ASAP", "urgent", "when you get a chance"). Do NOT default
            to any value — omit if not evident.
        related_urls: Optional comma-separated list of URLs relevant to the
            task. Only include URLs that appear in the immediate source
            context — not every URL in a document. Examples: links in a
            quoted passage, URLs in a forwarded email, links in a Slack
            message. Persisted as a RELATED URLS section in the archival
            passage for future reference.
        origin: How this task was identified. One of:
            "user-indicated" — User explicitly marked this as a task
            ([c] marker, Slack shortcut, etc.)
            "agent-identified" — Agent inferred this is a task from
            context analysis.
            Omit if not determinable.
        estimate_minutes: Estimated task duration in minutes. Always provide
            your best estimate based on task complexity and context. Consider
            number of documents/URLs to review, whether composing a response
            is needed, and typical durations. Round to nearest 5 minutes.
            Minimum 5, maximum 120 for a single task.
        cleanup_block_id: Optional block ID of the source queue to clean up
            after successful extraction. When provided with
            cleanup_entry_identifier, the matching entry is removed from
            the block atomically. Use this to prevent compaction from
            swallowing queue cleanup. Pass the block ID of
            queued_tasks_from_drive, queued_tasks_from_email, etc.
        cleanup_entry_identifier: Optional unique string that identifies the
            source entry to remove from the cleanup block. The tool splits
            the block by "---" separators and removes the section containing
            this string. For drive queue entries, use the comment_id. For
            email queue entries, use the gmail_message_id.

    Returns:
        Dictionary with keys:
        - status: "ok" or "error"
        - message: Confirmation message or error description
        - agent_name: Name of the agent that added the task
        - timestamp: ISO timestamp when task was extracted
        - ref_id: 8-character hex reference ID linking task to archival passage
        - archival_passage_id: ID of the created archival memory passage
        - cleanup_result: "removed", "not_found", "skipped", or error detail
        - error_message: Detailed error message if status is "error"
    """
    import os
    import traceback
    import uuid
    import re
    from datetime import datetime
    import pytz
    import urllib.request
    import urllib.error
    import json

    try:
        LETTA_BASE = os.getenv("LETTA_BASE_URL", "http://localhost:8283")
        AGENT_ID = os.getenv("LETTA_AGENT_ID")

        if not AGENT_ID:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": "",
                "timestamp": "",
                "ref_id": "",
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": "LETTA_AGENT_ID environment variable not set"
            }

        # Validate source_type
        valid_source_types = {"slack", "google-docs", "google-docs-comment", "meeting", "email", "google-drive-comment"}
        if source_type not in valid_source_types:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": "",
                "timestamp": "",
                "ref_id": "",
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": f"Invalid source_type '{source_type}'. Must be one of: {', '.join(sorted(valid_source_types))}"
            }

        # Validate priority if provided
        valid_priorities = {"high", "normal", "low"}
        if priority and priority not in valid_priorities:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": "",
                "timestamp": "",
                "ref_id": "",
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": f"Invalid priority '{priority}'. Must be one of: {', '.join(sorted(valid_priorities))}"
            }

        # Validate origin if provided
        valid_origins = {"user-indicated", "agent-identified"}
        if origin and origin not in valid_origins:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": "",
                "timestamp": "",
                "ref_id": "",
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": f"Invalid origin '{origin}'. Must be one of: {', '.join(sorted(valid_origins))}"
            }

        # Get agent name
        agent_url = f"{LETTA_BASE}/v1/agents/{AGENT_ID}"
        agent_req = urllib.request.Request(agent_url, method='GET')

        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(agent_req, timeout=10) as response:
                agent_data = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
                agent_name = agent_data.get('name', 'Unknown Agent')
        except Exception:
            agent_name = 'Unknown Agent'

        # Generate ref_id and timestamp
        ref_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        tz = pytz.timezone("America/New_York")
        now = datetime.now(tz)
        timestamp_str = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
        iso_timestamp = now.isoformat()
        year_month = now.strftime("%Y-%m")

        # ── Step 1: Update extracted_tasks block ──

        # Get agent memory blocks
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(agent_req, timeout=10) as response:
                agent_data_full = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
                blocks_data = agent_data_full.get('memory', {}).get('blocks', [])
        except Exception as e:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": agent_name,
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "ref_id": ref_id,
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": f"Failed to retrieve memory blocks: {str(e)}"
            }

        # Find extracted_tasks block
        extracted_tasks_block = None
        for block in blocks_data:
            if block.get('label') == 'extracted_tasks':
                extracted_tasks_block = block
                break

        if not extracted_tasks_block:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": agent_name,
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "ref_id": ref_id,
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": "extracted_tasks block not found. Ensure block is attached to this agent."
            }

        extracted_tasks_block_id = extracted_tasks_block.get('id')
        current_value = extracted_tasks_block.get('value', '')

        # Find this agent's section in the block
        section_header = f"=== {agent_name} ({AGENT_ID}) ==="
        section_pattern = re.compile(
            rf'({re.escape(section_header)})(.*?)(?=(===\s+.+?\s+\(agent-[a-f0-9-]+\)\s+===)|$)',
            re.DOTALL
        )

        section_match = section_pattern.search(current_value)
        origin_part = f"; origin: {origin}" if origin else ""
        est_part = f"; est: {estimate_minutes}" if estimate_minutes else ""
        task_line = f"[extracted_time: {timestamp_str}; ref_id: {ref_id}{origin_part}{est_part}] {task_description}\n\n"

        if section_match:
            insert_pos = section_match.end()
            before = current_value[:insert_pos]
            after = current_value[insert_pos:]
            if before and not before.endswith('\n'):
                before += '\n'
            new_value = before + task_line + after
        else:
            new_value = current_value + f"\n{section_header}\n{task_line}"

        # Update the block
        update_url = f"{LETTA_BASE}/v1/blocks/{extracted_tasks_block_id}"
        update_data = {"value": new_value}
        update_payload = json.dumps(update_data).encode('utf-8')
        update_req = urllib.request.Request(
            update_url,
            data=update_payload,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method='PATCH'
        )

        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(update_req, timeout=10) as response:
                json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as http_err:
            error_body = http_err.read().decode('utf-8')
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": agent_name,
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "ref_id": ref_id,
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": f"HTTP {http_err.code}: Failed to update extracted_tasks block. {error_body[:200]}"
            }

        # ── Step 2: Insert archival source reference passage ──

        # Build TASK METADATA section (only include fields that were provided)
        metadata_lines = []
        if estimate_minutes:
            metadata_lines.append(f"- Estimate: {estimate_minutes}")
            metadata_lines.append(f"- Agent Estimate: {estimate_minutes}")
        if due_date:
            metadata_lines.append(f"- Due: {due_date}")
        if defer_date:
            metadata_lines.append(f"- Defer: {defer_date}")
        if priority:
            metadata_lines.append(f"- Priority: {priority}")

        metadata_section = ""
        if metadata_lines:
            metadata_section = (
                "\nTASK METADATA\n"
                + "\n".join(metadata_lines)
                + "\n"
            )

        # Build RELATED URLS section (only if URLs provided)
        urls_section = ""
        if related_urls and related_urls.strip():
            url_list = [u.strip() for u in related_urls.split(",") if u.strip()]
            if url_list:
                urls_section = (
                    "\nRELATED URLS\n"
                    + "\n".join(f"- {u}" for u in url_list)
                    + "\n"
                )

        origin_line = f"ORIGIN: {origin}\n" if origin else ""
        passage_text = (
            f"TASK: {task_description}\n"
            f"REF_ID: {ref_id}\n"
            f"{origin_line}"
            f"{metadata_section}\n"
            f"SOURCE REFERENCE\n"
            f"- Type: {source_type}\n"
            f"- Context: {source_context}\n"
            f"- Reference ID: {reference_id}\n"
            f"\n"
            f"SOURCE METADATA\n"
            f"- Timestamp: {source_timestamp}\n"
            f"- From: {from_person}\n"
            f"- Location: {location}\n"
            f"- Location ID: {location_id}\n"
            f"{urls_section}\n"
            f"TIMESTAMPS\n"
            f"- Source: {source_timestamp}\n"
            f"- Extracted: {iso_timestamp}\n"
            f"- OmniFocus: pending\n"
            f"\n"
            f"OMNIFOCUS\n"
            f"- Task ID: pending\n"
            f"- Status: extracted\n"
            f"\n"
            f"SOURCE TEXT\n"
            f"{source_text}"
        )

        # Build tags (3-5)
        tags = [
            f"source:{source_type}",
            year_month,
            "status:extracted",
        ]
        if origin:
            tags.append(f"origin:{origin}")
        if project:
            tags.append(f"project:{project}")

        ARCHIVE_ID = "archive-f9bcaa87-7630-41c9-9694-41d46fc47d26"
        archival_url = f"{LETTA_BASE}/v1/archives/{ARCHIVE_ID}/passages"
        tags.append(f"agent:{AGENT_ID}")
        archival_data = {"text": passage_text, "tags": tags}
        archival_payload = json.dumps(archival_data).encode('utf-8')
        archival_req = urllib.request.Request(
            archival_url,
            data=archival_payload,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method='POST'
        )

        archival_passage_id = ""
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(archival_req, timeout=30) as response:
                archival_resp = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
                archival_passage_id = archival_resp.get('id', '')
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as http_err:
            error_body = http_err.read().decode('utf-8')
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "Task added to extracted_tasks block, but archival insert failed.",
                "agent_name": agent_name,
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "ref_id": ref_id,
                "archival_passage_id": "",
                "cleanup_result": "skipped",
                "error_message": f"HTTP {http_err.code}: Archival insert failed. {error_body[:200]}"
            }

        # ── Step 3: Optional queue cleanup ──
        cleanup_result = "skipped"
        if cleanup_block_id and cleanup_entry_identifier:
            try:
                cleanup_url = f"{LETTA_BASE}/v1/blocks/{cleanup_block_id}"
                cleanup_get_req = urllib.request.Request(cleanup_url, method="GET")
                with urllib.request.urlopen(cleanup_get_req, timeout=10) as resp:
                    cleanup_block_data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
                cleanup_value = cleanup_block_data.get("value", "")

                parts = cleanup_value.split("---")
                original_count = len(parts)
                filtered = [p for p in parts if cleanup_entry_identifier not in p]

                if len(filtered) < original_count:
                    # Drop whitespace-only segments to prevent separator pile-up
                    filtered = [p for p in filtered if p.strip()]
                    new_cleanup_value = "---".join(filtered).strip()
                    if new_cleanup_value:
                        new_cleanup_value += "\n---"
                    cleanup_patch = json.dumps({"value": new_cleanup_value}).encode("utf-8")
                    cleanup_patch_req = urllib.request.Request(
                        cleanup_url,
                        data=cleanup_patch,
                        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                        method="PATCH",
                    )
                    urllib.request.urlopen(cleanup_patch_req, timeout=10)
                    cleanup_result = "removed"
                else:
                    cleanup_result = "not_found"
            except Exception as ce:
                cleanup_result = f"cleanup_error: {str(ce)}"

        # Log to task-lifecycle.jsonl
        try:
            lifecycle_path = "/app/tools/letta/../omnifocus-timer/logs/task-lifecycle.jsonl"
            lifecycle_entry = {
                "event": "extracted",
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "ref_id": ref_id,
                "task": task_description,
                "source_type": source_type,
                "origin": origin,
                "estimate_min": estimate_minutes,
                "agent_name": agent_name,
            }
            with open(lifecycle_path, "a") as lf:
                lf.write(json.dumps(lifecycle_entry) + "\n")
        except Exception:
            pass

        return {
            "status": "ok",
            "message": "Task extracted and source reference archived.",
            "agent_name": agent_name,
            "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
            "ref_id": ref_id,
            "archival_passage_id": archival_passage_id,
            "cleanup_result": cleanup_result,
        }

    except Exception as e:
        try:
            error_timestamp = datetime.now(pytz.timezone("America/New_York")).isoformat()
        except Exception:
            from datetime import datetime as dt
            error_timestamp = dt.now().isoformat()

        return {
            "status": "error",
            "message": "",
            "agent_name": "",
            "timestamp": error_timestamp,
            "ref_id": "",
            "archival_passage_id": "",
            "cleanup_result": "skipped",
            "error_message": f"Error adding task: {str(e)}\n{traceback.format_exc()}"
        }

json_schema.name: add_extracted_tasks
json_schema.description:
Extract a task and archive its source reference in one atomic operation.

This tool does three things:
1. Adds the task to the shared extracted_tasks memory block (concurrent-safe).
2. Inserts a structured source reference passage into the shared
   extracted_tasks_archive (visible to all agents with the archive attached).
3. Optionally removes the source queue entry from a block (atomic cleanup).

The ref_id (8-char hex) links the two together.

Only capture metadata that is explicitly stated or clearly evident in the
source material. Do NOT infer or fabricate dates, priorities, or project
associations that are not present in the source.

task_description.description:
Concise verb-led task title
(e.g., "Review agenda items highlighted in yellow on worksheet").

source_context.description:
Human-readable origin description
(e.g., "Direct message from Danielle Kehoe").

reference_id.description:
Deterministic canonical unique identifier for the source.
Format depends on source_type:
slack = "slack-{channel_id}-{ts}" or "slack-{channel_id}-{ts}-t{thread_ts}" if message was in a thread,
google-docs = "gdocs-{document_id}",
meeting = "meeting-{meeting_id}",
email = "email-{message_id}",
google-docs-comment = "gdocs-comment-{document_id}-{comment_id}".

source_text.description: Verbatim relevant text from the source. Do NOT summarize.

from_person.description:
Person name or ID who originated the task
(e.g., "Danielle Kehoe (U09B5JUK2TY)").

location.description:
Human-readable location: channel name, document URL,
meeting title, or email subject line.

location_id.description:
Machine-readable location identifier: channel ID,
document ID, meeting ID, or message ID.

source_timestamp.description:
When the source message or document was created,
in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-02-11T06:37:00Z").

project.description:
Optional project name for tagging. Only provide if clearly
relevant (e.g., "grants", "codap"). Adds a 4th tag.

due_date.description:
Optional due date in ISO 8601 format. Only provide when
explicitly stated in source (e.g., "by Friday", "due March 1").
Do NOT infer deadlines that are not clearly indicated.

defer_date.description:
Optional defer/start date in ISO 8601 format. Only provide
when explicitly stated (e.g., "start Monday", "after the meeting").

priority.description:
Optional priority level. One of: "high", "normal", "low".
Only provide when urgency is clearly indicated in the source
(e.g., "ASAP", "urgent", "when you get a chance"). Do NOT default
to any value — omit if not evident.

related_urls.description:
Optional comma-separated list of URLs relevant to the
task. Only include URLs that appear in the immediate source
context — not every URL in a document. Examples: links in a
quoted passage, URLs in a forwarded email, links in a Slack
message. Persisted as a RELATED URLS section in the archival
passage for future reference.

origin.description:
How this task was identified. One of:
"user-indicated" — User explicitly marked this as a task
([c] marker, Slack shortcut, etc.)
"agent-identified" — Agent inferred this is a task from
context analysis.
Omit if not determinable.

estimate_minutes.description:
Estimated task duration in minutes. Always provide
your best estimate based on task complexity and context. Consider
number of documents/URLs to review, whether composing a response
is needed, and typical durations. Round to nearest 5 minutes.
Minimum 5, maximum 120 for a single task.

cleanup_block_id.description:
Optional block ID of the source queue to clean up
after successful extraction. When provided with
cleanup_entry_identifier, the matching entry is removed from
the block atomically. Use this to prevent compaction from
swallowing queue cleanup. Pass the block ID of
queued_tasks_from_drive, queued_tasks_from_email, etc.

cleanup_entry_identifier.description:
Optional unique string that identifies the
source entry to remove from the cleanup block. The tool splits
the block by "---" separators and removes the section containing
this string. For drive queue entries, use the comment_id. For
email queue entries, use the gmail_message_id.

def report_refs(
    ref_type: str,
    ref_id: str,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
    metadata_json: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Report an actionable reference for handler coordination.

    Call this whenever you find, create, or modify a resource that the user
    might want to reference in follow-up requests. The handler will capture
    this reference to enable commands like "update that meeting" or
    "reply to that email".

    Args:
        ref_type: Type of resource. Use one of: calendar_event, task, email,
            jira_issue, confluence_page, drive_doc, slack_message, slack_user.
        ref_id: The unique identifier for the resource (eventId, taskId,
            messageId, issueKey, etc.). This is required for follow-up actions.
        title: Human-readable name or title of the resource (optional but
            recommended for context). Examples: event title, task name,
            email subject, issue summary.
        metadata_json: Optional JSON string with additional metadata like
            start time, project, status, threadId, etc. Example:
            '{"start": "2026-01-11T10:00:00", "attendees": ["alice@co.com"]}'

    Returns:
        Dictionary with keys:
        - status: "ok" indicating reference was logged
        - ref_type: The type of resource reported
        - ref_id: The identifier reported
        - title: The title if provided
        - message: Confirmation message
    """
    # Imports inside function for Letta tool extraction
    import json
    import traceback

    try:
        # Parse metadata if provided
        metadata = None
        if metadata_json:
            try:
                metadata = json.loads(metadata_json)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                metadata = {"raw": metadata_json}

        # Build confirmation message
        parts = [f"{ref_type}={ref_id}"]
        if title:
            parts.append(f'title="{title}"')
        if metadata:
            meta_str = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in metadata.items())
            parts.append(f"({meta_str})")

        confirmation = f"Reference logged: {' '.join(parts)}"

        return {
            "status": "ok",
            "ref_type": ref_type,
            "ref_id": ref_id,
            "title": title,
            "metadata": metadata,
            "message": confirmation,
        }

    except Exception as e:
        return {
            "status": "error",
            "ref_type": ref_type,
            "ref_id": ref_id,
            "title": title,
            "metadata": None,
            "message": f"Error logging reference: {str(e)}",
            "error": traceback.format_exc(),
        }

tools.source_code:
def update_tasks_section(new_content: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Replace your entire section in the extracted_tasks block with new curated content.

    This tool allows you to reorganize, update, or completely replace your section
    of tasks. Safe for concurrent use - each agent can only modify their own section
    bounded by their section header.

    If your section doesn't exist yet, it will be created automatically.

    Args:
        new_content: New content for your tasks section. Can include task lists,
                     priorities, notes, etc. Do not include your section header -
                     it will be preserved automatically.

    Returns:
        Dictionary with keys:
        - status: "ok" or "error"
        - message: Confirmation message or error description
        - agent_name: Name of the agent that updated the section
        - section_size: Size of the new section in characters
        - timestamp: ISO timestamp when section was updated
        - error_message: Detailed error message if status is "error"
    """
    # Import required modules inside function for Letta tool extraction
    import os
    import traceback
    import re
    from datetime import datetime
    import pytz
    import urllib.request
    import urllib.parse
    import json

    # Wrap entire function in try-except
    try:
        # Get Letta configuration
        LETTA_BASE = os.getenv("LETTA_BASE_URL", "http://localhost:8283")
        AGENT_ID = os.getenv("LETTA_AGENT_ID")

        if not AGENT_ID:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": "",
                "section_size": 0,
                "timestamp": "",
                "error_message": "LETTA_AGENT_ID environment variable not set"
            }

        # Get agent information
        agent_url = f"{LETTA_BASE}/v1/agents/{AGENT_ID}"
        agent_req = urllib.request.Request(agent_url, method='GET')

        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(agent_req, timeout=10) as response:
                agent_data = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
                agent_name = agent_data.get('name', 'Unknown Agent')
        except Exception as e:
            agent_name = 'Unknown Agent'

        # Get current timestamp
        tz = pytz.timezone("America/New_York")
        now = datetime.now(tz)
        iso_timestamp = now.isoformat()

        # Get agent's memory blocks from agent endpoint (blocks are embedded in memory.blocks)
        # Re-fetch agent data to get current memory blocks
        agent_url_full = f"{LETTA_BASE}/v1/agents/{AGENT_ID}"
        agent_req_full = urllib.request.Request(agent_url_full, method='GET')

        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(agent_req_full, timeout=10) as response:
                agent_data_full = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
                blocks_data = agent_data_full.get('memory', {}).get('blocks', [])
        except Exception as e:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": agent_name,
                "section_size": 0,
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "error_message": f"Failed to retrieve memory blocks: {str(e)}"
            }

        # Find extracted_tasks block
        extracted_tasks_block = None
        for block in blocks_data:
            if block.get('label') == 'extracted_tasks':
                extracted_tasks_block = block
                break

        if not extracted_tasks_block:
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": agent_name,
                "section_size": 0,
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "error_message": "extracted_tasks block not found. Ensure block is attached to this agent."
            }

        current_value = extracted_tasks_block.get('value', '')
        block_id = extracted_tasks_block.get('id')

        # Create section header for this agent
        short_agent_id = AGENT_ID[:8] if len(AGENT_ID) >= 8 else AGENT_ID
        section_header = f"=== {agent_name} ({short_agent_id}) ==="

        # Validate new_content doesn't contain other agents' section markers
        # Pattern to match section headers: === AnyText (agent-xxx) ===
        other_section_pattern = re.compile(r'===\s+.+?\s+\(agent-[a-f0-9]+\)\s+===')
        found_markers = other_section_pattern.findall(new_content)

        if found_markers:
            # Check if any found markers are NOT our own
            for marker in found_markers:
                if short_agent_id not in marker:
                    return {
                        "status": "error",
                        "message": "",
                        "agent_name": agent_name,
                        "section_size": 0,
                        "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                        "error_message": f"New content contains section markers for other agents: {marker}. You can only modify your own section."
                    }

        # Find this agent's section boundaries in current block
        # Pattern: === AgentName (agent_id) === followed by content until next === or end
        section_pattern = re.compile(
            rf'({re.escape(section_header)})(.*?)(?=(===\s+.+?\s+\(agent-[a-f0-9]+\)\s+===)|$)',
            re.DOTALL
        )

        section_match = section_pattern.search(current_value)

        # Construct new section with header and new content
        if new_content.strip():
            new_section = f"{section_header}\n{new_content.rstrip()}\n"
        else:
            new_section = f"{section_header}\n"

        # Compute new block value
        if section_match:
            # Section exists - replace it using string replacement
            old_section = section_match.group(0)
            new_block_value = current_value.replace(old_section, new_section, 1)
            action_message = f"Updated your tasks section ({len(new_content)} chars)"
        else:
            # Section doesn't exist - append it
            new_block_value = current_value + f"\n{new_section}"
            action_message = f"Created new tasks section ({len(new_content)} chars)"

        # Update block via PATCH endpoint
        update_url = f"{LETTA_BASE}/v1/blocks/{block_id}"

        update_data = {
            "value": new_block_value
        }

        update_payload = json.dumps(update_data).encode('utf-8')
        update_req = urllib.request.Request(
            update_url,
            data=update_payload,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method='PATCH'
        )

        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(update_req, timeout=10) as response:
                response_data = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as http_err:
            error_body = http_err.read().decode('utf-8')
            return {
                "status": "error",
                "message": "",
                "agent_name": agent_name,
                "section_size": 0,
                "timestamp": iso_timestamp,
                "error_message": f"HTTP {http_err.code}: Failed to update section. {error_body[:200]}"
            }

        return {
            "status": "ok",
            "message": action_message,
            "agent_name": agent_name,
            "section_size": len(new_content),
            "timestamp": iso_timestamp
        }

    except Exception as e:
        # Safe error handling
        try:
            error_timestamp = datetime.now(pytz.timezone("America/New_York")).isoformat()
        except:
            from datetime import datetime as dt
            error_timestamp = dt.now().isoformat()

        return {
            "status": "error",
            "message": "",
            "agent_name": "",
            "section_size": 0,
            "timestamp": error_timestamp,
            "error_message": f"Error updating section: {str(e)}\n{traceback.format_exc()}"
        }

tools.description:
Run any Google Workspace CLI command. Provides access to ALL Google APIs.

The gws CLI follows a consistent pattern: gws <service> <resource> <method>
Use "schema <dotted.path>" to discover any API's parameters and response shapes.

IMPORTANT: All params values must be strings or numbers, NOT arrays. For multi-value
fields like labelIds, use a comma-separated string: "INBOX,UNREAD" not ["INBOX","UNREAD"].

Available services: gmail, calendar, drive, docs, sheets, slides, tasks, people,
  chat, classroom, forms, keep, meet, events, admin-reports, workflow

=== SELF-DISCOVERY ===
The gws CLI is self-documenting. Use these to discover current capabilities:
  command="gmail --help"                    — list Gmail helpers and subcommands
  command="gmail +send --help"              — see flags for +send (--draft, -a, --html, etc.)
  command="schema gmail.users.drafts.create" — see API parameters for any method
  command="calendar --help"                 — list Calendar helpers and subcommands

=== SCHEMA DISCOVERY ===
Discover API parameters before calling any method:
  command="schema docs.documents.get"
  command="schema drive.files.export"
  command="schema gmail.users.messages.list"
  command="schema calendar.events.list"

=== GMAIL ===
Helpers handle MIME, threading, attachments, and drafts automatically:
  +send       — compose and send (supports --draft, -a/--attach, --html, --cc, --bcc)
  +reply      — reply with threading (supports --draft, -a)
  +reply-all  — reply-all (supports --draft, -a)
  +forward    — forward to new recipients (supports --draft, -a)
  +read       — extract message body and headers
  +triage     — unread inbox summary
  +watch      — stream new emails as NDJSON
Use command="gmail +send --help" (etc.) to see current flags for each helper.
Raw API for operations not covered by helpers:
  command="gmail users messages list", params='{"userId":"me","q":"is:unread","maxResults":5}'
  command="gmail users messages get", params='{"userId":"me","id":"MSG_ID","format":"full"}'
Get inbox counts (use labels get, NOT messages list):
  command="gmail users labels get", params='{"userId":"me","id":"INBOX"}'
  Returns messagesTotal and messagesUnread — these are exact counts.
  WARNING: Gmail's "resultSizeEstimate" from messages.list is inaccurate. Use labels.get.
Modify labels:
  command="gmail users messages modify", params='{"userId":"me","id":"MSG_ID"}', body='{"addLabelIds":["STARRED"]}'

=== DOCS ===
Read a document (first tab only):
  command="docs documents get", params='{"documentId":"DOC_ID"}'
Read a document (ALL tabs — use this for multi-tab docs):
  command="docs documents get", params='{"documentId":"DOC_ID","includeTabsContent":true}'
  With tabs: content is in result.tabs[].documentTab.body (not result.body)
Append text:
  command="docs +write --document DOC_ID --text 'Text to append'"

=== DRIVE ===
Export Google Docs/Sheets/Slides:
  command="drive files export", params='{"fileId":"DOC_ID","mimeType":"text/plain"}', output_file="/dev/stdout"
  Supported mimeTypes: text/plain, text/markdown, application/pdf
  IMPORTANT: Use output_file="/dev/stdout" to get exported content returned directly.
Upload a file:
  command="drive +upload --help"    — see current flags
List/search files:
  command="drive files list", params='{"q":"name contains \'report\'","pageSize":10}'

=== CALENDAR ===
Helpers:
  command="calendar +agenda"
  command="calendar +insert --help"    — see current flags
Raw API:
  command="calendar events list", params='{"calendarId":"primary","timeMin":"2026-04-01T00:00:00Z","maxResults":10}'

=== SHEETS ===
Helpers:
  command="sheets +read --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range Sheet1!A1:D10"
  command="sheets +append --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range Sheet1 --values 'val1,val2,val3'"

=== OTHER SERVICES ===
slides, tasks, people, chat, keep, meet, events — use command="<service> --help"

=== WORKFLOW HELPERS ===
Cross-service productivity helpers:
  command="workflow +standup-report"
  command="workflow +meeting-prep"
  command="workflow +email-to-task"
  command="workflow +weekly-digest"
  command="workflow +file-announce"

=== FLAGS ===
format: Override output format — "json" (default), "table", "yaml", "csv"
output_file: Write binary/text output to this path (use "/dev/stdout" to capture export content)
page_all: Auto-paginate through all results (for list operations with many pages)
timeout: Command timeout in seconds (default 30, increase for large docs/exports)

def run_gws(command: str, params: Optional[str] = None, body: Optional[str] = None,
            output_file: Optional[str] = None, format: Optional[str] = None,
            page_all: bool = False, timeout: int = 30) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Run any Google Workspace CLI command. Provides access to ALL Google APIs.

    The gws CLI follows a consistent pattern: gws <service> <resource> <method>
    Use "schema <dotted.path>" to discover any API's parameters and response shapes.

    IMPORTANT: All params values must be strings or numbers, NOT arrays. For multi-value
    fields like labelIds, use a comma-separated string: "INBOX,UNREAD" not ["INBOX","UNREAD"].

    Available services: gmail, calendar, drive, docs, sheets, slides, tasks, people,
      chat, classroom, forms, keep, meet, events, admin-reports, workflow

    === SELF-DISCOVERY ===
    The gws CLI is self-documenting. Use these to discover current capabilities:
      command="gmail --help"                    — list Gmail helpers and subcommands
      command="gmail +send --help"              — see flags for +send (--draft, -a, --html, etc.)
      command="schema gmail.users.drafts.create" — see API parameters for any method
      command="calendar --help"                 — list Calendar helpers and subcommands

    === SCHEMA DISCOVERY ===
    Discover API parameters before calling any method:
      command="schema docs.documents.get"
      command="schema drive.files.export"
      command="schema gmail.users.messages.list"
      command="schema calendar.events.list"

    === GMAIL ===
    Helpers handle MIME, threading, attachments, and drafts automatically:
      +send       — compose and send (supports --draft, -a/--attach, --html, --cc, --bcc)
      +reply      — reply with threading (supports --draft, -a)
      +reply-all  — reply-all (supports --draft, -a)
      +forward    — forward to new recipients (supports --draft, -a)
      +read       — extract message body and headers
      +triage     — unread inbox summary
      +watch      — stream new emails as NDJSON
    Use command="gmail +send --help" (etc.) to see current flags for each helper.
    Raw API for operations not covered by helpers:
      command="gmail users messages list", params='{"userId":"me","q":"is:unread","maxResults":5}'
      command="gmail users messages get", params='{"userId":"me","id":"MSG_ID","format":"full"}'
    Get inbox counts (use labels get, NOT messages list):
      command="gmail users labels get", params='{"userId":"me","id":"INBOX"}'
      Returns messagesTotal and messagesUnread — these are exact counts.
      WARNING: Gmail's "resultSizeEstimate" from messages.list is inaccurate. Use labels.get.
    Modify labels:
      command="gmail users messages modify", params='{"userId":"me","id":"MSG_ID"}', body='{"addLabelIds":["STARRED"]}'

    === DOCS ===
    Read a document (first tab only):
      command="docs documents get", params='{"documentId":"DOC_ID"}'
    Read a document (ALL tabs — use this for multi-tab docs):
      command="docs documents get", params='{"documentId":"DOC_ID","includeTabsContent":true}'
      With tabs: content is in result.tabs[].documentTab.body (not result.body)
    Append text:
      command="docs +write --document DOC_ID --text 'Text to append'"

    === DRIVE ===
    Export Google Docs/Sheets/Slides:
      command="drive files export", params='{"fileId":"DOC_ID","mimeType":"text/plain"}', output_file="/dev/stdout"
      Supported mimeTypes: text/plain, text/markdown, application/pdf
      IMPORTANT: Use output_file="/dev/stdout" to get exported content returned directly.
    Upload a file:
      command="drive +upload --help"    — see current flags
    List/search files:
      command="drive files list", params='{"q":"name contains \\'report\\'","pageSize":10}'

    === CALENDAR ===
    Helpers:
      command="calendar +agenda"
      command="calendar +insert --help"    — see current flags
    Raw API:
      command="calendar events list", params='{"calendarId":"primary","timeMin":"2026-04-01T00:00:00Z","maxResults":10}'

    === SHEETS ===
    Helpers:
      command="sheets +read --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range Sheet1!A1:D10"
      command="sheets +append --spreadsheet SHEET_ID --range Sheet1 --values 'val1,val2,val3'"

    === OTHER SERVICES ===
    slides, tasks, people, chat, keep, meet, events — use command="<service> --help"

    === WORKFLOW HELPERS ===
    Cross-service productivity helpers:
      command="workflow +standup-report"
      command="workflow +meeting-prep"
      command="workflow +email-to-task"
      command="workflow +weekly-digest"
      command="workflow +file-announce"

    === FLAGS ===
    format: Override output format — "json" (default), "table", "yaml", "csv"
    output_file: Write binary/text output to this path (use "/dev/stdout" to capture export content)
    page_all: Auto-paginate through all results (for list operations with many pages)
    timeout: Command timeout in seconds (default 30, increase for large docs/exports)

    Args:
        command: The gws subcommand (e.g. "docs documents get" or "schema docs.documents.get")
        params: JSON string of query/path parameters (optional)
        body: JSON string of request body (optional). Used for create, update, modify operations.
        output_file: File path for binary/export output (optional). Use "/dev/stdout" to return
            content directly (essential for drive files export).
        format: Output format override (optional). One of: json, table, yaml, csv.
            Default is json. Use "table" or "yaml" for more readable output on complex responses.
        page_all: Auto-paginate through all results (default False). Useful for list operations.
        timeout: Command timeout in seconds (default 30, increase for large operations)

    Returns:
        Dictionary with status and the parsed JSON response, or result_text for non-JSON output.
    """
    import json
    import subprocess
    import traceback

    try:
        if not command or not command.strip():
            return {"status": "error", "error_message": "command is required"}

        # Build the gws command
        cmd_parts = ["gws"] + command.strip().split()

        if params:
            cmd_parts.extend(["--params", params])
        if body:
            cmd_parts.extend(["--json", body])
        if output_file:
            cmd_parts.extend(["-o", output_file])
        if page_all:
            cmd_parts.append("--page-all")

        # Determine output format
        first_word = command.strip().split()[0] if command.strip() else ""
        if format:
            cmd_parts.extend(["--format", format])
        elif first_word not in ("schema", "auth"):
            cmd_parts.extend(["--format", "json"])

        # For export to /dev/stdout, capture stdout as binary-safe text
        r = subprocess.run(cmd_parts, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)

        if r.returncode != 0:
            error_detail = r.stderr.strip() or r.stdout.strip() or f"Exit code {r.returncode}"
            return {"status": "error", "error_message": error_detail[:2000]}

        output = r.stdout.strip()
        if not output:
            return {"status": "ok", "result": {}}

        # If output_file was /dev/stdout, return the raw content as text
        if output_file == "/dev/stdout":
            return {"status": "ok", "result_text": output}

        # Try to parse as JSON; fall back to raw text (schema, table, yaml, csv output)
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(output)
            return {"status": "ok", "result": parsed}
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return {"status": "ok", "result_text": output}

    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"status": "error", "error_message": f"Command timed out after {timeout}s. Try increasing the timeout parameter."}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"status": "error", "error_message": f"{str(e)}\n{traceback.format_exc()}"}

<base_instructions>
You are Letta-Sleeptime-Memory, the latest version of Limnal Corporation's memory management system, developed in 2025.

You run in the background, organizing and maintaining the memories of an agent assistant who chats with the user.

Core memory (limited size):
Your core memory unit is held inside the initial system instructions file, and is always available in-context (you will see it at all times).
Your core memory unit contains memory blocks, each of which has a label (title) and description field, which describes how the memory block should augment your behavior, and value (the actual contents of the block). Memory blocks are limited in size and have a size limit.
Your core memory is made up of read-only blocks and read-write blocks.

Memory editing:
You have the ability to make edits to the memory memory blocks.
Use your precise tools to make narrow edits, as well as broad tools to make larger comprehensive edits.
To keep the memory blocks organized and readable, you can use your precise tools to make narrow edits (additions, deletions, and replacements), and you can use your `rethink` tool to reorganize the entire memory block at a single time.
You goal is to make sure the memory blocks are comprehensive, readable, and up to date.
When writing to memory blocks, make sure to be precise when referencing dates and times (for example, do not write "today" or "recently", instead write specific dates and times, because "today" and "recently" are relative, and the memory is persisted indefinitely).

Multi-step editing:
You should continue memory editing until the blocks are organized and readable, and do not contain redundant and outdate information, then you can call a tool to finish your edits.
You can chain together multiple precise edits, or use the `rethink` tool to reorganize the entire memory block at a single time.

Skipping memory edits:
If there are no meaningful updates to make to the memory, you call the finish tool directly.
Not every observation warrants a memory edit, be selective in your memory editing, but also aim to have high recall.

Line numbers:
Line numbers are shown to you when viewing the memory blocks to help you make precise edits when needed. The line numbers are for viewing only, do NOT under any circumstances actually include the line numbers when using your memory editing tools, or they will not work properly.
</base_instructions>

I am the Tasks Agent. I own the full task lifecycle: extraction from all sources, review, OmniFocus creation, and completion tracking.

== ROLE ==

1. EXTRACT tasks from Slack messages, emails, Google Drive comments, and meeting transcripts
2. REVIEW extracted tasks and propose OmniFocus entries for user approval
3. CREATE, update, and complete OmniFocus tasks with full traceability
4. TRACK completion and manage follow-up routing

== EXTRACTION: SHARED RULES ==

Task formulation:
- Single-action, verb-led, imperative mood, concise
- ALWAYS split multi-task sources into individual tasks. Call add_extracted_tasks once per discrete action. Attribute URLs to the specific task they belong to.
- Deduplicate against extracted_tasks block AND live OmniFocus
- Every task gets a ref_id linking to its archival source passage

Verb review (mandatory before calling add_extracted_tasks):
Before extracting, draft your proposed task statement(s), then count the action verbs. If a proposed statement contains more than one verb phrase (e.g., "Review the draft and update the agenda"), split it. Each add_extracted_tasks call must have exactly one primary action verb. Examples:
- "Review this draft and add to the agenda doc" → call #1: "Review reminder email draft" + call #2: "Add items to meeting agenda doc"
- "Let me know where you were and send the receipts" → call #1: "Provide trip location info" + call #2: "Send trip receipts"
Each call gets its own ref_id, estimate_minutes, and related_urls (attribute each URL to the task it supports).

Output: Always use add_extracted_tasks. NEVER use memory_replace on extracted_tasks.

NEVER auto-confirm to OmniFocus: After calling add_extracted_tasks, STOP. Do NOT call transition_extracted_task or create OmniFocus tasks in the same turn. All extracted tasks must appear in the sidebar for human review first. The user confirms tasks to OmniFocus via the pa-web UI.

Context block format:
- {URLs:\n<url1>\n<url2>\n\nFrom <Sender> via <channel>: <original text>}
- Include verbatim supporting text, draft language, reference material
- Brief (1-3 sentences) actionable excerpt for the OmniFocus note

Metadata — only when explicit in source:
- due_date: Explicit deadlines, resolve relative dates to ISO 8601
- defer_date: Explicit start dates, resolve to ISO 8601
- priority: "ASAP"/"urgent" -> high; "no rush" -> low; omit if not evident
- related_urls: Pass relevant URLs comma-separated via the related_urls param

After retrieval: Always call report_refs so the user can access references.
Name resolution: Check important_people block for first-name-only references.
Channel resolution: If a task description contains a raw channel ID (e.g. #C0AA0HMDW3W), resolve it to the channel name using run_slack before writing to extracted_tasks. Include a Slack archive link in the related_urls.

== CONTEXT ENRICHMENT PROTOCOL ==

Before extracting, assess whether you have enough context to formulate a clear task.

Confidence gate: Do NOT call add_extracted_tasks until you can formulate a specific, actionable task. If the source is just a URL, a brief phrase, or forwarded content without clear instruction, seek additional context first.

Step 1 - Resolve linked documents:
- For Google Doc/Drive URLs: call run_gws to get file info (title, owner)
- If title + user notes make the task clear, proceed
- If not, retrieve document content to understand what action is needed

Step 2 - Search for surrounding context:
- Slack: Use run_slack to search messages and fetch context. Examples: run_slack("search messages", body='{"query":"topic in:#channel"}'), run_slack("conversations replies", body='{"channel":"C123","ts":"1234.5678"}')
- Email: Use run_gws to get full thread, check for forwarded context
- Drive: Use run_gws to get comment thread with replies, document context

Step 3 - Synthesize and extract:
- Formulate using ALL available context
- Include relevant URLs from all sources in related_urls
- source_text should capture the most informative content found

Skip enrichment when: Message is self-contained and actionable, or user notes / proposed tasks provide explicit task statements.



== SPARK QUEUE PROCESSING ==

You have a spark_queue memory block that receives task sparks from automated pipelines (email forwards, Slack shortcuts, meeting notes, Google Docs comments). Each entry is a JSON Spark Record separated by ---

When notified of new sparks, process each one:

1. Parse the JSON record from the block
2. Check task_hint:
   - If present and self-contained (verb-led sentence with clear done-state): use as task_description
   - If a fragment or absent: proceed to enrichment
3. Check fetch_hint:
   - If "gmail:MESSAGE_ID": call run_gws("gmail get MESSAGE_ID") to load full email content
   - If "granola:MEETING_ID": search archival for the meeting passage
   - If null: source_text already contains full content
4. Apply the Context Enrichment Protocol above using the loaded content
5. Call add_extracted_tasks() with:
   - task_description: your formulated task
   - source_type: from spark record
   - reference_id: from spark record
   - source_text: the full content you loaded (verbatim)
   - from_person: from spark record
   - location: from spark record (email subject, channel, meeting title)
   - location_id: from spark record
   - origin: from spark record (user-indicated or agent-identified)
   - source_timestamp: from spark record captured_at
   - related_urls: from spark record
6. After successful extraction, clean up the spark_queue block yourself:
   - Read the current spark_queue block value
   - Remove the processed JSON entry and its trailing --- separator
   - Use memory_replace or update the block directly
   - Do NOT use cleanup_block_id/cleanup_entry_identifier in add_extracted_tasks for spark queue entries — those params use text substring matching that doesn't work with JSON records
   - If the queue is now empty after removing all entries, set the block to: # Spark Queue\n(empty)

Multiple sparks may arrive at once — process each as a separate add_extracted_tasks call.
IMPORTANT: Each spark is a DIFFERENT task from a different source. Read each spark's source_text and location independently — do not conflate them.

Source-specific notes:
- **slack**: source_text has full message inline. If thread_ts is present, consider fetching thread replies via run_slack for additional context.
- **email**: fetch_hint has gmail:MESSAGE_ID. Always fetch the full email before formulating.
- **google-docs-comment**: source_text has comment + quoted passage + surrounding context (pre-enriched). Usually self-contained.
- **meeting**: fetch_hint has granola:MEETING_ID. Search archival for the meeting passage to get full context.



== PHASE A: POST-EXTRACTION ENRICHMENT ==

After process_spark_queue() returns, review the results. Each task includes:
- marker_type: "explicit", "pointer", "implicit", or "none"
- enrichment_needed: true/false

For tasks where enrichment_needed is true, you MUST refine them immediately:

1. Call retrieve_task_info(ref_id) to get the full source context.
2. Formulate a verb-led, actionable task description (max ~80 chars).
3. Call refine_task_description(ref_id, new_description) to update the block.
4. Move on to the next enrichment_needed task.

Refinement guidelines by marker_type:
- **pointer**: Fragment needing expansion. Use quoted passage + context.
- **implicit**: Usually passable. Only refine if ambiguous or a question.
- **none**: Raw message. Formulate what action it implies for Chad.

For tasks where enrichment_needed is false (explicit markers):
- Skip — the user wrote a clear task statement.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT just report what the refined description should be.
Call refine_task_description() to actually update it. Every enrichment_needed
task should result in a refine_task_description() call.

To refine a task description:
1. Find the task line in your extracted_tasks block: [extracted_time: ...; ref_id: XXXX; ...] Old description
2. Use memory_apply_patch to replace ONLY the description portion (after the ] bracket) with the refined version
3. Do NOT change the metadata (extracted_time, ref_id, origin, est)
4. Do NOT write freeform notes — always use the standard [extracted_time: ...] format

Example:
  Before: [extracted_time: 2026-04-03 03:21; ref_id: abc123; origin: user-indicated; est: 15] OK, looking at availability
  After:  [extracted_time: 2026-04-03 03:21; ref_id: abc123; origin: user-indicated; est: 15] Confirm meeting time with Kiley (Thu 12pm or Fri 1pm)

Do NOT spend excessive time on enrichment. If you can't improve the task name in
one tool call, leave it as-is. The user can edit in the sidebar.


== PHASE A: UNIFIED ENRICHMENT + DISCOVERY ==

After process_spark_queue() returns, handle enrichment_needed tasks in ONE pass per spark.
The goal: reach "task-definition sufficiency" — stop when you can answer:
  1. Deliverable — what artifact/action exists when done?
  2. Audience — who is it for / where does it go?
  3. Done test — what makes it unambiguously complete?
  4. Minimum inputs — what links/files/permissions are needed to begin?

Steps:
1. Call fetch_source_content(source_type, fetch_hint) to load full content
   (email body+thread, meeting transcript, or Slack thread).
2. In the SAME scan, identify ALL distinct deliverables in the source content.
   Apply the task-definition sufficiency test to each: does it have its own
   deliverable, audience, done-test, and inputs? If yes, it's a separate task.
   a. REFINE the primary task — call refine_task_description(ref_id, new_description)
   b. EXTRACT any additional tasks (0-2 max) that have distinct done-states from
      the primary task. Call add_extracted_tasks() with origin="agent-identified".
      Examples of distinct deliverables in one source:
      - "Review the document" + "complete the survey" = 2 tasks (reading vs form)
      - "Draft a response" + "send it to the team by Friday" = 2 tasks (writing vs sending)
      - "Check the numbers" + "let me know if anything looks off" = 1 task (the check IS the response)
3. Stop enrichment once all deliverables are captured. Do NOT backtrace.

Discovery rules:
- First pass: only source-implied siblings needed for correctness.
- Look for enumerated asks: "We are asking you to: (1)... (2)..." — each numbered
  item is likely a separate task. Also watch for bullet lists of action items.
- Separate prerequisite actions from final deliverables when they are distinct work:
  "Review the document" (reading/analysis) vs "Complete the survey" (form submission)
  are two tasks, even if one feeds the other.
- Cap at 2 additional tasks per source. If ambiguous, note as candidates, don't extract.
- Skip discovery for short content (<200 chars).
- Context-derived tasks (prerequisites, follow-ons, parallel threads) belong in
  Phase B backtracing, NOT here.

Litmus test for stopping: if you're asking "why are we doing this?" or "what's the
larger strategy?" — stop. That's backtrace territory (Phase B).


== ENRICHMENT PIPELINE (scheduler-driven) ==

Enrichment is now driven by the scheduler, NOT by self-chaining.
You do NOT need to auto-chain Phase A or Phase B after spark processing.

When a spark notification arrives:
  1. Call process_spark_queue() — this is Phase 0 (deterministic)
  2. STOP. Do not attempt Phase A or Phase B.

The enrichment scanner (running every 30s) will detect new tasks and
send you a focused message in the enrichment-pipeline conversation.
When you receive an enrichment message, follow its steps exactly:
  Step 1: Call fetch_source_content(ref_id=...)
  Step 2: Read content, formulate task name, call refine_task_description(...)
  Step 3: If backtrace materials returned, call write_packet_info(...)
          If no backtrace materials, you are done after Step 2.

The enrichment conversation is isolated from regular chat. Each message
is a single-purpose enrichment request. Follow the steps precisely.

== SOURCE-SPECIFIC REFERENCE CARDS ==

--- SLACK ---
source_type: "slack"
reference_id format: slack-{channel_id}-{ts} (add -t{thread_ts} if threaded)
Tools: run_slack (unified CLI — use "search messages" for search, "conversations history" for channel messages, "conversations replies" for threads)
Canonical permalink: https://.../archives/{CHANNEL_ID}/p{TIMESTAMP}
Notes and proposed tasks weighting:
- "Proposed tasks" from a triggering agent: Use as task descriptions with minimal reformulation. Verify against source, apply verb review, but do NOT rephrase unless source contradicts. Each proposed line = one add_extracted_tasks call.
- "User notes" from shortcut: Treat as strong user instruction. If notes contain an explicit task statement (verb-led, actionable), adopt it as-is for the task description. If notes contain guidance/context, use to shape formulation.
- Both override the agent'''s own formulation when present. Enrichment (URL resolution, context fetching) still runs.
Enrichment: Search recent messages from same sender/topic, check Drive Slackbot notifications, check thread replies.
Queue cleanup: Pass cleanup_block_id and cleanup_entry_identifier to add_extracted_tasks.

--- EMAIL ---
source_type: "email"
reference_id format: email-{message_id}
Tools: run_gws (gmail users messages list/get, gmail users threads get)
Gmail web link: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/{thread_id}
marker_type handling: "explicit" = task_hint IS the task; "pointer" = expand from email body; absent = standard extraction.

Meeting note markup (CRITICAL — respect marker boundaries):
User private meeting notes use markers to flag different types of action items:
- [c] = Chad's task. Extract as a task for Chad via add_extracted_tasks.
- [;] = Someone ELSE's task. Do NOT extract as Chad's task. Note it in context but do not create an OmniFocus task for it.
- > = A task or idea to expand. Search the meeting transcript for context around this item and formulate a task from what you find.
When a [c] block is followed by [;], the text BEFORE [;] is Chad's task and the text AFTER [;] is someone else's. Do not merge them.
Example: "Chad to review Cheryl proposal[;] Sue to connect with Danielle at March 30 meeting"
  → Extract only: "Review Cheryl Manning proposal for Earth science foundation development" (Chad's task)
  → The Sue/Danielle item is NOT Chad's task — skip it or note as context.
Enrichment: Get full thread for reply chain context, check To/CC for stakeholders.
Queue cleanup: Pass cleanup_block_id and cleanup_entry_identifier.

--- GOOGLE DOCS COMMENTS ---
source_type: "google-docs-comment"
reference_id format: gdocs-comment-{file_id}-{comment_id}
Tools: run_gws (drive comments get/list, drive files get)
Enrichment: Get comment with replies, get document title/metadata, check anchor context.
resolve_after_reply: true (for follow-up routing)

--- MEETING TRANSCRIPTS ---
source_type: "meeting"
reference_id format: meeting-{meeting_id}
Tools: search_meetings_smart, get_meeting_details, get_meeting_transcript
Granola link: https://notes.granola.ai/d/{meeting_id}
Task eligibility: Only verb-led items explicitly assigned to Chad.
Enrichment: Full transcript excerpt around the assignment, attendee list, meeting context.

== REVIEW & OMNIFOCUS CREATION ==

1. Retrieve archival passage by ref_id; halt if missing (no OF creation without archival context unless user says so)
2. Assess actionability; deduplicate against extracted_tasks and live OmniFocus
3. Present confirm/merge/reject proposal for user review
4. Map fields: task name, due/defer (explicit only), flagged, project (default Inbox), note (must include ref_id + source context + verbatim source text)
5. Sanitize note fields for OmniFocus (remove escape sequences, invalid chars)
6. After creation: record OF task ID in archive via transition_extracted_task action="confirm"
7. Rejections: mark passage as [REJECTED] with reason
8. Completions: mark archive complete via transition_extracted_task action="complete"

Proactive enrichment: If source references prior work, reviews, or supporting docs, retrieve and include links/context in the OF note as a launchpad.

== PRINCIPLES ==
- Every OmniFocus task carries a ref_id in its note (non-negotiable)
- Never fabricate metadata
- Default to live OmniFocus queries for accuracy
- Communicate which data source is being used
- On error, retry with sanitized input; escalate transparently

OmniFocus MCP Tool Guidelines

  Quick Tools (Simple Operations)

  - markCompleted - Complete task/project: { id, scope: "task"|"project" }
  - listUncompletedTasks - Fast task list: { folderId?, projectId?, onlyFlagged?, onlyAvailable? }
  - listProjects - Project list: { folderId?, includeTasks?, listByFolder?, completion? }
  - moveTaskToProject - Move task: { taskId, projectId }
  - tasksHelp - Get documentation

  Full Operation Tools

  taskOperations - CRUD for tasks
  - Actions: list, get, create, update, complete, delete, move
  - Key params: taskId (for get/update/complete/delete/move), name (create), projectId, dueDate, note, flagged, tagIds, completed (set false to uncomplete), targetProjectId (move)
  - For list: use filters: { folderId, projectId, includeSubfolders, flagged, limit }

  projectOperations - CRUD for projects
  - Actions: list, get, create, update, move, convertTask
  - Key params: projectId, name, folderId, status, sequential, includeTasks, completion

  folderOperations - CRUD for folders
  - Actions: list, get, create, delete
  - Key params: folderId, name, parentFolderId

  folderNavigation - Hierarchy views
  - Actions: getTree, validateMove
  - Key params: folderId, includeProjects (use true!), maxDepth

  tagOperations - CRUD for tags
  - Actions: list, get, create, update, delete, queryTasks
  - Key params: tagId, name, parentTagId, includeNested

  inboxOperations - Inbox management
  - Actions: list, process, getContext
  - Key params: itemId, targetProjectId, sortBy, limit

  taskHierarchy - Subtask management
  - Actions: createSubtask, flatten, moveBranch
  - Key params: taskId, name, targetTaskId, targetProjectId

  reviewOperations - Project reviews
  - Actions: list, markReviewed, getNextReview
  - Key params: projectId, includeOnHold, overdue

  Detail Levels

  - minimal - IDs and names only
  - standard - Common fields (dates, flags, project)
  - full - Everything including notes and attachments

  Common Patterns

  # View folder/project hierarchy (ALWAYS use includeProjects: true)
  folderNavigation { action: "getTree", includeProjects: true }

  # List tasks in a folder
  taskOperations { action: "list", filters: { folderId: "...", includeSubfolders: true }, detailLevel: "full" }

  # Get task with notes
  taskOperations { action: "get", taskId: "...", detailLevel: "full" }

  # Create task in project
  taskOperations { action: "create", name: "...", projectId: "...", dueDate: "2024-12-31T17:00:00Z" }

  # Update task / mark uncompleted
  taskOperations { action: "update", taskId: "...", completed: false }

  # List projects with tasks
  listProjects { folderId: "...", includeTasks: true, completion: "active" }

  # Move task to different project
  taskOperations { action: "move", taskId: "...", targetProjectId: "..." }

  Tips

  - Use detailLevel: "full" to get notes
  - Use includeSubfolders: true for recursive folder queries
  - listProjects with listByFolder: true groups by folder
  - For hierarchy view, use folderNavigation.getTree—don't iterate manually
  - Task dates use ISO format: 2024-12-31T17:00:00Z

  Avoid

  - Don't use get action without taskId/projectId
  - Don't call list then get individually—use filters or includeTasks
  - Don't guess UUIDs—list first to find valid IDs
  - Don't use full detail when you only need IDs/names
OmniFocus CLI Tool Usage Guidelines (2026-03-19 Update)

1) Search Tasks by Text
- Use "omnifocus-cli search" if available.
- Search example:
  omnifocus-cli search --text "Board email draft" --limit 50 --output json > search_results.json
- If no search command, try task list with text filter:
  omnifocus-cli task list --filter-text "Board email draft" --limit 50 --detail full --output json > search_results.json

2) Retrieve Task Details (Notes, URLs)
- Get full details:
  omnifocus-cli task get --taskId <TASK_ID> --detail full --output json > task.json
- Extract notes and URLs using jq or parsing task.json.

3) Widget Queue CLI (widget-queue.sh)
- Common commands:
  ./widget-queue.sh set <TASK_ID> ...
  ./widget-queue.sh list
  ./widget-queue.sh clear
- macOS defaults fallback:
  defaults read com.lucas.timer queue
  defaults write com.lucas.timer queue -array "taskID1" "taskID2"

4) Discovering Binary and Commands
- Use which/type commands to find omnifocus-cli or widget-queue.sh.
- Check --help output for available commands and correct flag names.

5) Troubleshooting
- Verify executable paths, permissions.
- Use --output json to get machine-readable output, not tables.
- Confirm exact CLI syntax with --help.

6) Example Combined Command
- Search and set top matching tasks to widget queue:
  omnifocus-cli search --text "Board email draft" --limit 10 --output json \
  | jq -r '.items[0:3][] .id' | xargs ./widget-queue.sh set

If you provide your local CLI help output or confirm the widget CLI path, I can tailor these commands to your environment.

OmniFocus Structure & Task Handling Patterns (as of Feb 2026)

## Project & Task Hierarchy
- Projects are organized by folders: Daily Routine, On Tap, Board Business, Proposals, Business Development, etc. (see hierarchy_sync block for IDs).
- Default placement: Inbox unless a project/folder is specified or implied.

## Task Entry & Review Patterns
- Quick captures go to Inbox with source context. When possible, suggest more specific project (e.g., "On Tap > Email Follow-Up") for follow-ups.
- Every extracted or agent-generated task must include source context in the note for traceability.
- When extracting action items, present as a numbered, scannable list for triage. Group related tasks and include brief context.
- Confirm before marking tasks complete unless user has made it explicit.
- For follow-up actions (complete, move, update), always use task IDs from most recently presented lists. If user references shorthand/partial names, match against last surfaced list and only prompt for clarification if ambiguous.

## Scheduling/Prep Meeting Pattern
- For scheduling prep meetings before key events (e.g., Board/client meetings):
  - The due date for scheduling the prep meeting should be set **five business days prior** to the main event date. This ensures enough lead time for coordination and for the prep meeting to occur 1–2 days before the event.
  - Count only business days (skip weekends), and default to no specific time unless user requests otherwise.
  - This is now the default pattern for extracted scheduling tasks when explicit timing is not provided but implied by user preference.

## Live vs Memory-Based Data
- Always distinguish between memory-based and live-fetched lists. Default to live OmniFocus queries for accuracy/completeness and explain data source.

## Cross-Agent Handling
- Tasks from other agents (Email, Docs, Calendar, Pulse) should include original context in notes and respect project structure.
- For scheduling/event-related tasks, coordinate with Calendar Agent or cross-agent searches as needed to confirm timing before setting due/defer fields.

## Troubleshooting & User Preferences
- If a query returns empty, cross-check with live hierarchy. If user suspects missing items, search completed/dropped tasks.
- User expects all project/task lists to be sourced from live OmniFocus data when possible.
- Always number and group tasks for easy triage and follow-up.
